\begin{lemma}\label{cor:bernoulli}
Let
\[
 p=\lceil\log_2(3000r)\rceil,
 \qquad
 r\ge2(4p+1)^{1000}.
\]
For \(0<\eta<1\), \(0<\theta\le1/2\), and
\(\kappa=n\theta\ge64K_0r/\eta^2\), the exact random projection \(P\)
and independent Bernoulli coordinate projection \(E\) satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bernoulli-bound}
 \Prob\{\norm{\theta^{-1}X^TEX-I_r}>\eta\}\le1/1000.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

entries.exact_context_tex:
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:graph}
Let a connected finite multigraph have positive even degrees. Assign
a matrix of operator norm at most one to each edge, with compatible
coordinate dimensions at its endpoints. Suppose one edge matrix is a
real rank-\(r\) orthogonal projection \(P_0=VV^T\), \(r\ge1\).
At each vertex also allow a coordinate weight of absolute value at most
one. The contraction of Definition~\ref{def:graph-contraction},
given by \eqref{eq:graph-contraction}, has absolute value
at most \(r\).
\end{lemma}

conjuncts.expected_statement: For q≥1 arbitrary real scalar random variables on a probability space with every joint moment appearing finite: moment equals sum over partitions of products of block cumulants.

For a finite nonempty occurrence set I, partition tau into q≥1 nonempty prescribed product groups and arbitrary repeated real factors with requisite joint products integrable: cumulant of products equals the sum of factor cumulant products over sigma with sigma join tau one block.
Joint cumulant is additive and real-homogeneous in each argument, with all moments in each formula finite.
Cumulant vanishes if its arguments split into two nonempty independent groups (independence of vectors of arguments, not just pairwise independence).
For q≥2 adding arbitrary deterministic real constants to each argument leaves cumulant unchanged.
For odd q≥1 and a real Z symmetric about zero with requisite moments finite, cum(Z,...,Z)=0.
